content: Self-love is the greatest of all flatterers.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: Think of an opinion or dispute you've recently defended. How might subtle self-love be flattering you into believing you were purely noble?
